subject: Request: temporary quota elevation & billing path for BrightByte
messages:
From: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@brightbyte.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightbyte.com
Date: 2026-05-21T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Spike next week — temporary quota lift request

Evelyn —

We're seeing an unexpected-but-healthy spike in usage tied to an in-app campaign that starts Monday. Our ingest for the MVP is 4x the baseline for short windows (bursty traffic from webhook fans). Can Redwood provision an additional 200k token quota/day for 7 days and tell us how billing will be handled? Procurement needs an estimate to open a PO — we can approve a short-term charge or take credits against next month's invoice.

Attached: BrightByte_MVP_traffic_report.csv (csv, 12KB) — shows projected hourly token churn.

Questions from our end:
- Can you guarantee the increase without changing our model variant?
- Will this be billed pro-rata on usage or as a flat uplift line item?
- Any option to lock a capped price for the 7-day window?

Appreciate a quick path — campaign is time-sensitive.

Thanks,
Tom Reilly
Head of Platform, BrightByte
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@brightbyte.com>
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike next week — temporary quota lift request

Tom —

Thanks for the heads up and the traffic dump — that's helpful. Short answer: we can support a 200k token/day uplift for a 7-day window. Two pragmatic billing options below — pick whichever works for procurement:

Option A — On-demand uplift (fastest)
- We enable a temporary quota ceiling immediately.
- Billed on next invoice as a usage line (pro-rated actuals).
- Rate: our standard overrun rate + 10% premium to cover burst capacity allocation.

Option B — Prepaid uplift (discounted, requires PO)
- Prepay a 7-day uplift slab (we invoice a single credit for the estimated uplift).
- 20% discount on the uplift slab if BrightByte commits to convert 50% of the uplift into a 3-month committed bump after the campaign.

We generally don't change model variants for short windows — we'll keep the same model/variant unless you tell us otherwise. To lock price we can issue a provisional quota addendum (one-page) that Laura can sign and attach to the PO. I'll also need an approximate daily peak (your CSV suggests 200-260k/day at the high end) and whether KV cache and prefix caching are enabled on your side (saves cost).

If you want me to put Option B into a one-page agreement I can do that today.

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@brightbyte.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbyte.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-22T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike next week — temporary quota lift request

Ben —

Appreciate the quick options. Procurement prefers a PO + a single-line prepay if it reduces churn in approval. Two quick clarifications:
1) If we prepay and then convert 50% to a 3-month commit (your Option B), will the unused portion of the prepaid slab be refundable or credited?
2) We need a firm cap price to put on the PO — can you lock the uplift slab at the discounted rate for 48 hours while we route the PO?

procurement@brightbyte.com: 
- We can sign a one-page addendum and provide a PO if Redwood sends the DocuSign link and an invoice estimate (net-30).

On our end: KV cache is enabled and prefix caching is in play for ~40% of traffic. Peak estimates here: 220k tokens/day for the week window.

Thanks — Tom

> > Tom —
> >
> > Thanks for the heads up and the traffic dump — that's helpful. Short answer: we can support a 200k token/day uplift for a 7-day window...
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: procurement@brightbyte.com, Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@brightbyte.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-23T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike next week — temporary quota lift request

Tom / Procurement team —

Happy to coordinate the PO and DocuSign flow. Practical path that usually moves fastest:

1) I will create a one-page "Provisional Quota Agreement" (attached: provisional_quota_agreement.pdf) that includes:
   - uplift slab: 220k tokens/day for 7 days
   - capped uplift spend estimate at discounted slab rate (Option B pricing shown)
   - conversion language: if BrightByte converts 50% into a 3-month commit, we'll apply the 20% discount to that portion; any unused prepaid credit is applied as a billing credit against the following invoice (no refunds).
2) We send DocuSign to the signatory you designate and issue an invoice (net-30) for the prepaid slab. The invoice will be a separate line item titled "Provisional Quota Top-up — BrightByte (Campaign May 2026)" to make procurement clearance straightforward.
3) If procurement needs the charge to be captured against a PO number, include PO# in the DocuSign signature page and we'll mirror that PO on the invoice.

Irene — quick ask: can you confirm there are no security or routing caveats if we open temporary capacity for BrightByte (short-lived allocation, same model variant)?

Tom — attaching the provisional_quota_agreement.pdf for review. If the terms look good I can start the DocuSign flow this afternoon and Ben will enable the uplift once we have a signed doc/PO.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: provisional_quota_agreement.pdf (pdf, 22KB)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@brightbyte.com>, procurement@brightbyte.com
Date: 2026-05-25T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike next week — temporary quota lift request

Team —

I'm comfortable approving a one-time concession to help BrightByte through their campaign. Final decisions below so ops/billing are aligned:

- Approved: Option B (prepaid uplift slab) at a 15% discount (we'll meet them halfway from the 20% ask).
- Billing instruction: invoice as a separate prepayment line; include PO# when provided; do not apply to recurring committed invoice by default — apply credit only if they convert.
- Unused prepaid credit: apply as a credit to the next invoice (no cash refunds).
- Legal/signature: Laura, ship DocuSign for the provisional_quota_agreement.pdf and capture signatory name + PO#.
- Enablement: Ben, you can enable the quota on signature + invoice upload. Coordinate with Ops for a temporary allocation window (7 days starting on first call usage).

Irene: accept the short-lived allocation from the security side and confirm once Ops is cleared.

Tom / Procurement: we'll lock the discounted slab price for 48 hours from this timestamp. Please confirm signatory and PO# ASAP so Laura can send DocuSign.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
